# Sirach Chapter 38 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_038_page_001.jpg

---

**38:1** Honor the physician with the honor due him, according to your need for him, for the Lord created him;

**38:2** healing comes from the Most High, and the physician receives gifts from the king.

**38:3** The physician's skill makes him stand tall, and he is admired in the presence of the great.

**38:4** The Lord created medicines from the earth, and the sensible person will not refuse them.

**38:5** Was not water made sweet by a piece of wood, so that his power might become known to all?

**38:6** And he gave skill to human beings so that he might be glorified in his wondrous works.

**38:7** By them the physician removes pain and heals, and the apothecary compounds his remedies.

**38:8** There is no end to his works, and from him comes health over all the earth.

**38:9** My child, when you are ill, do not neglect yourself, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.

**38:10** Turn aside from wrongdoing and make your hands do right, and cleanse your heart from all iniquity.

**38:11** Offer a sweet-smelling sacrifice and a cereal offering of fine flour, and pour oil on your offering, as much as you can afford.

**38:12** Then give the physician his proper place, for the Lord created him as well; do not let him leave you, for there is need of him.

**38:13** There are times when recovery lies entirely in the hands of physicians,

**38:14** for they too will pray to the Lord to grant them success in relieving pain and in healing — for the sake of the patient's life.

**38:15** Whoever sins against his Maker, let him fall into the hands of the physician.

**38:16** My child, shed tears over one who has died, and begin your lamentation as one who is suffering greatly; wrap the body as befits a person, and do not neglect the burial.

**38:17** Let your weeping be bitter and your wailing fervent; observe the mourning befitting a person's station, for one day or two, to avoid criticism; then be comforted for your grief.

**38:18** For grief can lead to death, and grief of heart drains away one's strength.

**38:19** Grief lingers when calamity comes, and the life of the poor wears down the heart.

**38:20** Do not give your heart to grief; drive it away and remember your own end.

**38:21** Do not forget: there is no coming back; you cannot help him, and you can only harm yourself.

**38:22** "Remember my fate, for yours is the same: mine was yesterday, and yours is today."

**38:23** When the dead is at rest, let his memory also rest; be comforted for him once his spirit has left.

**38:24** The wisdom of the scribe depends on the opportunity for leisure; and only a person who has little business to attend to can become wise.

**38:25** How can one who holds the plow become wise, who takes pride in wielding the goad, who drives oxen and is absorbed in their work, and whose conversation is all about cattle?

**38:26** He devotes his attention to making his furrow straight, and is kept busy providing fodder for the heifers.

**38:27** So too is every craftsman and skilled artisan who spends their nights as well as their days at work; those who engrave seal designs, intent on producing a faithful likeness, who apply their hearts to completing their work.

**38:28** So too is the smith, sitting at his forge, intent on his iron-work; the breath of fire scorches his flesh, and he contends with the heat of the furnace; the noise of the hammer rings in his ears; his eyes are fixed on the design of the piece; he applies his heart to finishing it, and stays up late to polish it.

**38:29** So too is the potter, sitting at his work and turning the wheel with his feet; he is in constant worry over his work, and all his work is measured out.

**38:30** He shapes the clay with his arm and treads it soft with his feet; he applies his heart to completing the glazing, and keeps watch to clean the kiln.

**38:31** All of these trust in their hands, and each one is skilled in his own craft.

**38:32** Without them a city cannot be built, and there can be neither settlement nor population.

**38:33** Yet they are not sought for the city's ruling council, nor do they gain prominence in the public assembly. They do not occupy the judge's seat, nor do they understand legal decisions; they cannot expound principles or give judgment, nor are they found among those who speak in parables.

**38:34** But they uphold the fabric of this age, and their petition is in the skill of their craft.
